keyboard.label: Keyboard
home.nextChar: Next character: "{ch}" – it is added once you have {acc} % in the last {n} characters of a lesson and recognise the newest character reliably and fast. From the 5th character on, progress is confirmed in the next session (at least 3 h later).
home.allChars: You have all characters of the set!
home.allCore: You have all {n} characters of the main programme! Rare punctuation (the extension) can be turned on in Settings.
home.lessonInfo: {min} min · character {wpm} WPM · spacing {fwpm} WPM · tone {freq} Hz
home.speedProposal: The coach suggests a pace of {wpm}/{fwpm} WPM. {why} (Change it in Settings.)
home.loadDayWarn: Already {min} min today. Above {max} min a day little more is gained – better continue tomorrow.
home.loadSessionEnd: This session has lasted {min} min. I recommend stopping and continuing after a longer break.
home.loadFatigue: The last lesson showed fatigue – take a break of at least {min} min, the next session will then start with a warm-up.
home.copyDesc: Characters run as a stream without waiting – type as you go, even a character or a whole word later. Now: {name}, {gap}, {speed} WPM. Scoring aligns the whole line, the correction comes at its end.
home.copyWordLag: Goal of this step: a whole-word lag – type a word while the next one sounds; the ✓/✗ mark comes 2 words later.
home.copyMobile: On a phone I recommend typing each whole word only after it has finished.
audio.failed: Could not turn the sound on.

intro.remember: Remember the sound. You can play it again.
discrim.question: Can you recognise the new character among similar ones?
lesson.fluency: Fluency block: known characters faster ({wpm}/{fwpm} WPM). Not counted in the result.
lesson.warmup: Warm-up – known characters first, to see what you remember.
lesson.rewarm: Warm-up after the break – known characters only for a while.
fatigue.whyTtr: For over a minute your reaction has been {pct} % slower than at the start of the session.
fatigue.whyAcc: For over a minute your accuracy has been {pp} points lower than at the start of the session.
fatigue.advice: That is usually fatigue – a short break (3–5 min: stand up, stretch, have a drink) usually helps more than more drill.
pause.rewarm: After the break you start with {s} s of warm-up with known characters.
pause.hint: Lesson time is stopped. After a break of at least {min} min the lesson starts with a short warm-up.
fatigue.noteEvent: Fatigue showed during the lesson ({what} than at the start of the session). Take a longer break before the next lesson – at least {min} min, or continue tomorrow.
fatigue.noteEndTtr: Towards the end of the lesson your reaction slowed down compared with the start of the session – possibly fatigue. Take a break before the next lesson.
fatigue.noteEndAcc: Towards the end of the lesson your accuracy dropped compared with the start of the session – possibly fatigue. Take a break before the next lesson.
fatigue.noteThirdTtr: Towards the end of the lesson your reaction slowed down by {pct} % – possibly fatigue. Take a break before the next lesson.
fatigue.noteThirdAcc: Towards the end of the lesson your accuracy dropped by {pp} points – possibly fatigue. Take a break before the next lesson.
verdict.confirm: Excellent, {pct} %! The character "{ch}" will be confirmed in the next session (in {h} h or tomorrow) – memory consolidates it over a break and sleep. Then the next character is added.
verdict.advance: Excellent! {pct} % in the last {n} characters. The next lesson adds the character "{ch}".
verdict.full: Excellent! {pct} % – you have the whole set.
verdict.few: Adding a character needs at least {n} characters in a lesson (now {trials}).
verdict.acc: Adding a character needs {need} % in the last {n} characters (now {pct} %). Continue with the same set – a plateau is normal.
verdict.ttrUnstable: {pct} % overall, but your reaction slowed down towards the end ({slower} %). The character is added once the reaction is stable – try again after a break.
verdict.newFew: {pct} % overall, but the new character "{ch}" sounded only {n}× ({need}× needed). Try a longer lesson.
verdict.newAcc: {pct} % overall, but the new character "{ch}" only {acc} % ({need} % needed). Practise it some more.
verdict.newSlow: {pct} % overall, but you react more slowly to the new character "{ch}" ({ttr} ms, others {others} ms). Practise it some more so that you recognise it instantly.
result.gapEase: Part of the lesson ran with longer gaps (accuracy dropped below 75 %) – that is fine, the coach gives you more time to recognise characters.
result.slowDay: Today you react {pct} % slower than usual on the same characters – probably tiredness. A short lesson or sleep helps more than long training; tomorrow will be better.
result.fluency: Fluency block: {pct} % at {wpm}/{fwpm} WPM (not counted in the result).
result.fluencyTtr: Fluency block: {pct} % at {wpm}/{fwpm} WPM, reaction {ttr} ms (not counted in the result).
result.warmupDrop: – a slight drop after a break is normal, it is not a regression; it evens out during the lesson.
result.warmupOk: – that is how well you remember the characters.
result.loadDayWarn: Already {min} min today. More than {max} min a day adds little – better continue tomorrow.
result.loadSessionEnd: The session has lasted {min} min – after {max} min concentration drops. I suggest stopping; what you learned consolidates over a break and sleep.
result.loadSession: Session {min} min. Take at least a 30 s break before the next block.

dndTip.title: Turn on Do not disturb
dndTip.text: Notifications and calls interrupt the lesson sound and your focus. Before training, turn on Do not disturb on your phone (and turn it off after the lesson).
dndTip.android: Android: swipe down from the top of the screen and tap “Do not disturb”.
dndTip.samsung: Samsung: swipe down twice from the top and tap “Do not disturb”.
dndTip.iphone: iPhone: open Control Center (swipe down from the top-right corner) → Focus → Do Not Disturb.
verdict.aborted: The lesson was interrupted by closing or reloading the page. It was saved, but without advancing to the next character.
plan.entryTest: Returning or active operator: the entry test on Home (or in Settings) finds out which characters you know and suggests where to start.
dash.title: Progress and regularity
dash.empty: The overview appears after the first synchronization with the server.
dash.legend: Darker = more minutes; full colour = daily goal reached ({target} min).

dash.fatigue14.one: In the last 14 days fatigue showed in {n} lesson. Shorter blocks with breaks and training when rested help.
dash.fatigue14.other: In the last 14 days fatigue showed in {n} lessons. Shorter blocks with breaks and training when rested help.

dash.accNote: The coach keeps the lesson accuracy around 85 %, so do not expect a steady rise here – progress shows in characters and reaction.
dash.ttrNote: ms from the end of the character to the key press – lower is better. After a character is added it usually rises for a while.
dash.warmTip: warm-up {warm}, end of the previous session {prev}
dash.warmNote: Accuracy in the first 90 s of a session – the best measure of what you remember over a break and sleep.
dash.copyAccNote: Copy-behind lessons. The ladder step goes up after 2 sessions ≥ 90 %, after 2 sessions below 75 % it gets easier.
dash.lagNote: How many characters behind the sender you type. A longer and stable lag is the goal – your head holds more characters, in U4 whole words.
stats.title: Koch path
stats.intro: From the last {n} lessons. Learned {level} of {of} characters. Colour = accuracy, number = median reaction. Tap a character for details.
stats.empty: No data yet – statistics appear after the first lesson is sent.
stats.nextHint: This character is added once you meet the conditions for advancing.
stats.noConf: You have not confused "{ch}" with anything.
copy.phaseWordLag: feel free to type a whole word later
copy.phaseAbbr: abbreviations and Q codes only from those mastered in the vocabulary trainer ({n}) – words fill the rest
copy.locked: Copy behind unlocks once you have mastered at least {n} characters in character lessons (now {m}) – first as a trial, fully from level U3.
copy.listen: Listen and type – do not wait for the end.
copy.fatAcc: Accuracy in the last lines is {pp} points lower than at the start of the lesson.
copy.fatMiss: In the last lines {pp} points more characters are missing than at the start – the stream is running away.
copy.fatAdvice: That is usually fatigue – a short break (3–5 min: stand up, stretch, have a drink) usually helps more than more lines.
copy.legend: Sent on top, typed below. Green correct, red underlined a confusion, orange "_" missing, struck through extra.
copy.legendMask: Grey: characters drowned by the band (fading, another station, a static crash) – {n}, not counted.
copy.maskNote: Another {n} characters were drowned by the band – they are not scored (neither as errors nor as correct).
copy.verdictMid: {acc} after alignment – a good range for learning. The next step comes from 90 % in 2 sessions.
copy.verdictLow: {acc} after alignment. Copying behind is a new skill – it is fine to type a word only after it has finished. After two sessions below 75 % the coach makes the step easier.
copy.lagDetail: Lag: median {lag} ch. ({ms} ms after the end of the character), 90 % of characters within {p90} ch., at most {max} ch.
copy.fatNote: During the lesson the coach suggested a break because of possible fatigue.
copy.drift: Towards the end of the lesson the lag grew by {n} ch. – try to type as you go so that the stream does not run away.
copy.counts: Correct {ok}, confusions {sub}, missing {del}, extra {ins} (of {n} sent characters, {rounds} lines).
copy.loadSessionEnd: The session has lasted {min} min – after {max} min concentration drops. I suggest stopping.
about.title: About
about.intro: A free Morse code receiving trainer. Author: OK2MTW.
about.licence: The app is free software under the licence EUPL-1.2 (European Union). You may use, study, modify and distribute it free of charge. If you make a modified version available to other people (even just over a network), you must make its source code available under the same licence.
about.morsePro: © Stephen C. Phillips – text to Morse conversion and timing (WPM, Farnsworth). EUPL-1.2. github.com/scp93ch/morse-pro, author of the website morsecode.world.
about.methodText: The Koch method (Ludwig Koch, 1936) and the character order of LCWO.net (Fabian Kurz, DJ5CW); Farnsworth timing; instant character recognition (ICR) training after morsecode.world and CWops CW Academy; findings on differences between learners (Long Island CW Club). We do not take over texts and content of these projects – only principles.
demo.title: Try it – three characters
demo.text: A short beginner lesson with the characters K, M and U, about a minute. You hear a character and answer by tapping the keyboard below (on a PC also with the keyboard). Nothing is saved.
demo.sound: Turn the sound on; headphones are best.
demo.noAudio: Sound could not be started – try again.
demo.listen: This is how this character sounds ({i}/{n})
demo.noAnswers: No answers – never mind, try again.
demo.reaction: Typical reaction {ms} ms after the end of the character
demo.more: In real training the coach adds characters one by one, adjusts the pace and watches for fatigue, and your progress is saved. Accounts are created by invitation only.
demoBand.title: This is how the band sounds
demoBand.text: The goal of the training: understand a real contact even in noise and interference. Listen to a sample – the text appears exactly when a character has sounded (in training you do not see it, of course, you write it yourself).
demoBand.goal: The training leads here step by step: from two characters through the whole alphabet, words and abbreviations to a contact in interference. The coach watches your pace and fatigue. Accounts are by invitation only for now.
news.title: What's new
news.i18n: The app now speaks English too. Switch the language in the menu under the user icon → Settings → Language; it applies to your other devices as well.
news.demo: Demo without an account: the login page has a “Try it” tab – a one-minute lesson with three characters. Feel free to send the link to friends so they can try Morse code.
news.extraChars: The main programme now has 44 characters. The rare punctuation , ' : ) " @ ! is hardly used in amateur radio – it is an optional extension you can turn on in Settings → “Learn the extension too”. The prosigns KN, AS, BT and AR stay in the main programme.
news.earlyCopy: You can try copy behind before level U3: from 10 mastered characters Home shows a “Copy behind (trial)” card – groups from your characters only. Character lessons stay the main thing; copy behind starts fully at U3 and continues where you stop.
auth.serverBusy: The server is not responding right now ({msg}) – you are training offline, results will be sent later.
register.tryAgain: The invitation may be fine – try again.
band.title: Band sound (listening test)
band.settingsHint: In development: noise, fading, interference and real keying – coaches only. Nothing is stored.
band.intro: Pick a situation and listen. Judge whether it sounds like a real band – what is overdone, what is missing, what disturbs unnaturally. The text is a random QSO line, you do not need to copy it.
band.adjustHint: Changes apply from the next line.
band.presetHint.clean: As in the lessons – for comparison.
band.presetHint.weak: A station just above the noise, 500 Hz filter.
band.presetHint.qsb: The signal slowly fades out and comes back (short-wave fading).
band.presetHint.flutter: Fast strength variation, typical of polar paths.
band.presetHint.qrn: Atmospheric discharges – short crashes, mostly in summer on the lower bands.
band.presetHint.qrm: Two more stations close to the frequency, wide 2400 Hz filter – you hear them all.
band.presetHint.qrmNarrow: The same interference with a narrow 250 Hz filter – neighbours get weaker.
band.presetHint.hand: Irregular dot and dash lengths as with a straight key, harder edge.
band.presetHint.chirp: The tone “chirps” at key-down and the whole transmission slowly drifts – an older transmitter.
band.presetHint.evening: Everything at once, mildly: noise, fading, static, two stations, hand keying.

news.vocab: New training alongside Morse: amateur radio abbreviations, Q codes and call sign prefixes. On Home, the “Abbreviations, Q codes and prefixes” card – an overview to browse and a quiz with three answers, no time limit. The error rate of each list is in Progress.
news.vocabCopy: Abbreviations and Q codes in copy behind (from level U4) now come only from those you have mastered in the “Abbreviations, Q codes and prefixes” trainer. What you learn in the quiz, you then hear in Morse.
news.nav: New layout: Copy behind and Abbreviations have their own buttons in the top bar next to Home. Progress is in the menu under the user icon.

home.headDesc: A QSO is played once – type nothing, just listen and remember. Then write its key data (call, RST, name, QTH…). Now: {name}.
home.headMobile: You answer with the normal phone keyboard, without a time limit.
head.pauseHint: An interrupted QSO is not scored. Lesson time is stopped.
head.verdictMid: {acc} correct answers – a good zone for learning. The next step comes from 90 % in 2 sessions.
head.verdictLow: {acc} – hard for now. Never mind: listen to the whole QSO and repeat the data in your mind; a step back comes by itself after 2 sessions below 75 %.
head.short: A session counts for progress from {n} questions.
headResult.title: Head-copy lesson result
news.head: Head copy (U6): a QSO is played once, nothing is typed, then you write its key data – call, RST, name, QTH. As a trial from level U4 on the Copy screen, the whole ladder (30–45 WPM, also on the band) from U5; 40 WPM without interference leads to level U6 Master.

entry.title: Entry test – I already know CW
entry.cardText: Every character is played twice in random order, you answer on the keyboard. The test suggests how many characters to start with, so you do not begin with K M.
entry.settingsHint: Already know CW? The entry test finds out which characters you know.
entry.howTo: Type every character you hear. Nothing is corrected during the test – if you do not know, just wait (6 s).
entry.result: You know {known} of {n} characters (both tries correct within {ms} ms). In the Koch order the first {level} in a row.
entry.resultNext: Lessons start there – the next new character will be {ch}.
entry.resultAll: You have the whole main programme – the coach takes you to full speed and then to copy behind.
entry.unsure: Unsure or slow: {list} – they come one by one as new characters (with an introduction).
entry.keepHigher: Back to Home (you already have {n} characters)
news.entry: Entry test for those who already know CW: every character twice, the app suggests how many characters to start with (on Home for returning operators, otherwise in Settings).
key.title: Telegraph key (experimental)
key.settingsHint: Sending: keyer with sidetone – keyboard or USB key converter (default Left/Right Ctrl) and two on-screen paddles. Experimental, coaches only for now.
key.paddlesHint: Hold a button like a paddle; two fingers at once = both paddles (squeeze). The sound starts with the first touch.
key.outHint: The decoder learns your rhythm from the neighbouring elements (dot and dash lengths and the gaps inside characters, between characters and words) – you do not have to keep the set tempo.
key.rec.hint: Recording for tuning the decoder: write what you sent, then send it. Only the tone times are sent (and the last exercise tasks).
key.rec.placeholder: What you sent, e.g. CQ TEST
key.rec.sent: Sent, thanks. Press Clear the transcript for another attempt.
key.rec.fail: Could not send – try again (the recording waits in the queue).
key.typeHint.iambicB: Both paddles alternate dot and dash; releasing both during an element adds one more opposite element.
key.typeHint.iambicA: Both paddles alternate dot and dash; after release only the element being sent is finished.
key.typeHint.single: One lever: dots to one side, dashes to the other, no alternation.
key.typeHint.bug: Dots automatic (dot side), dashes by hand – the tone lasts while you hold the dash side.
key.typeHint.straight: The tone lasts while you hold the key (dot contact / Key button); you set the lengths yourself.
key.sidetoneHint: (switch off when the converter has its own buzzer)
key.logHint: Time from the first event and the gap to the previous one in ms (browser timestamp). Shows lost and doubled events and the spread; the converter delay is measured with an oscilloscope.
send.ex.intro: Tasks from the characters you know from receiving ({n}); a series of {tasks} tasks. Nothing is saved yet.
send.ex.wait: After sending wait a moment (about 2 s), or Done (Enter).
send.ex.review: The task above, what was read from your sending below.
send.focus.good: All within the target range – this task is right.
send.focus.ratio.low: Dashes were only {v}× longer than dots (target 3×) – hold the dash longer.
send.focus.ratio.high: Dashes were {v}× longer than dots (target 3×) – release the dash sooner.
send.focus.inGap.low: Gaps between elements inside a character were short ({v}× dot, target 1×) – the elements run together.
send.focus.inGap.high: Gaps between elements inside a character were long ({v}× dot, target 1×) – the character may split in two.
send.focus.charGap.low: Gaps between characters were short ({v}× dot, target 3×) – characters run together; wait a moment after each one.
send.focus.charGap.high: Gaps between characters were long ({v}× dot, target 3×) – they may sound like word gaps.
send.focus.wordGap.low: Gaps between words were short ({v}× dot, target 7×) – words run together.
send.focus.wordGap.high: Gaps between words were long ({v}× dot, target 7×).
send.focus.stability: The tempo varied ({v} %, target up to 15 %) – try a little slower and evenly.
